mutation_battery.note: Mutation (b) SURVIVED the first attempt and that is recorded rather than smoothed over. The correction-chain test used distinct created_at values, so it never exercised the comparator's tiebreak and `>` passed. The gap was in the test, not the implementation: a tie-ordering test was added, asserting both page orders because a one-order test passes by luck half the time, and the mutation is now caught. A surviving mutation is evidence the assertion is weak, never evidence the condition is unprovable.

production_measurement.note: The population and the settlement row count are what make pagination mandatory rather than precautionary: 37496 settlement rows over 25430 distinct picks average 1.47 rows per pick, and the average is not the bound -- a correction chain is unbounded, so any chunk can exceed PostgREST's 1000-row page. A truncated page does not raise; it silently omits picks, which reads as 'no settlement exists' and makes the caller settle an already-settled pick. The earlier form of this note said 'a 500-pick chunk can hold far more than PostgREST's default 1000-row page', which conflated a ROW cap with the BYTE cap that actually sets the chunk size: 500 ids produce a 19630-byte request line against the ~8 KiB proxy header buffer, so 500 was never a legal chunk. The chunk is now 98, derived in packages/db/src/runtime-repositories.ts and asserted against a real query builder.

coverage_gap.why_it_matters: An under-read is the fail-OPEN direction: an omitted pick reads as 'no settlement exists' and the caller re-settles it. This is the exact class `Require live-DB proof for runtime changes` names (UTV2-519, UTV2-521).
coverage_gap.guard_state: `Require live-DB proof for runtime changes` is RED on this PR and is CORRECT. It is not the recorded #1479 false positive: no t1-proof file for UTV2-1886 exists on main or on this branch. It is not one of the four required checks, so it blocks no merge.
coverage_gap.landed_remedy: apps/api/src/t1-proof-utv2-1886-settlement-batch.test.ts, committed and present at the bound head. Test 1 builds three settled picks (1, 2 and 3 settlements chained through corrects_id) plus a deliberately unsettled control and asserts the real DatabaseSettlementRepository's findLatestForPicks agrees id-for-id with findLatestForPick, omits the unsettled pick, and returns exactly the settled count -- this is what proves .in() completeness and the ordering agreement against real PostgREST. Test 2 reads the same six-row, two-pick population at pageSize 1000, 1 and 2 and asserts all three maps are identical and match the single-pick path -- this is what proves later-page settlements are not missed. Test 3 reads three picks at chunkSize 1 and asserts the per-chunk results union rather than replace. The suite is gated on SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and deletes no rows.
coverage_gap.scope_consequence: file_scope_lock is settable only at `ops:lane-manifest create` and this lane declared five files, so three of the five paths in this lane's diff sit outside it: apps/api/src/t1-proof-utv2-1886-settlement-batch.test.ts (the new suite), package.json (the only test:t1-proof:live wiring point -- pnpm verify fails closed with WIRING_TEST_UNWIRED_NEW on an unreachable test file), and docs/05_operations/db-writer-classification.json (scripts/ci/db-writer-inventory.ts discovers the file on its createDatabaseRepositoryBundle marker and rejects it unregistered; that validator runs at .github/workflows/ci.yml:243 INSIDE the required `verify` job, so this third path is not optional -- omitting it would turn a required check red). A lock cannot be widened by an agent and a scope-override/v1 is a CODEOWNERS artifact that is never self-authored. Measured on #1565 at 485cc944b the two scope checks DISAGREE and the disagreement is correct: `File scope lock` is RED and `Lane authority` is GREEN, because they read different sources. `Lane authority` evaluates the lane TYPE contract, and .lane/lanes/runtime.yml admits all three paths -- apps/api/** (:5), docs/05_operations/db-writer-classification.json (:42) and package.json (:48), the last two registered there by UTV2-1842 for exactly this case. `File scope lock` and `Return review packet` evaluate this lane's MANIFEST lock, pinned at ops:lane-manifest create to the five implementation files. An earlier draft of this bundle predicted both checks RED; that prediction was wrong about `Lane authority` and is corrected here from the measurement. None of the three is one of the four required checks, and each is reporting a real fact rather than a defect.
